# READ THIS FIRST IF THE GATES ALL COME BACK UNVERIFIABLE. They will on any
# checkout without a built bin/aowlparser and a native nifler at the path
# tests/diff.sh and tests/stress.sh look for -- which is a Linux path. Run here
# on Windows they answer `total=225 pass=0 ... oracle-skip=225`: a zero that
# means "no oracle", not "everything failed". Each of those rows therefore
# carries a GUARD regex (`oracle-skip=[1-9]`) that turns that answer into
# UNVERIFIABLE rather than a disagreement. Getting this wrong is not a detail:
# a checker that read `pass=0` as a measurement would report 184/184 as WRONG,
# and the next person to "fix" the README would write in a number no gate had
# printed. That is the exact defect this file exists to stop.
# The one row that runs anywhere is the DENOMINATOR -- `ls tests/corpus/*.nim`.
# It is also the row that caught the live defect: the README said "all 169
# corpus programs pass -- 154 of them byte-for-byte" while the dialect table
# eight sections down said 172/172, and the directory holds 172 files.
# UNATTRIBUTED rows fail the run on purpose; that class is where a number lives
# when NO command produces it. Six of them are the jsonfast engineering notes and
# the "full Nim compiler test corpus (2890 files)" paragraph. They are not
# guessed at and not deleted here: they are listed, so the next person either
